description: The line plot illustrates the performance of two large vision-language models—GPT-4o and Claude-3.5-Sonnet—in terms of Accuracy@1 (%) as a function of the number of child nodes (tree width) in a multimodal tree search framework, as presented in the paper “VisuoThink: Empowering LVLM Reasoning with Multimodal Tree Search.” The x-axis, labeled “Num. of Child Nodes (Tree Width),” is linear and ranges from 1 to 7, with tick marks at integer values. The y-axis, labeled “Accuracy@1 (%)”, is also linear, spanning from 15% to 35%, with major gridlines every 5 percentage points. The GPT-4o model is represented by a solid blue line with circular markers; its accuracy starts at 24.4% at tree width 1, rises to 28.9% at width 3, peaks at 34.4% at width 5, and then declines to 31.1% at width 7. The Claude-3.5-Sonnet model is shown with a dashed light blue line and cross markers; it begins at 26.7% at width 1, increases slightly to 27.8% at width 3, then decreases steadily to 24.4% at width 5 and further to 20.0% at width 7. The plot visually contrasts the two models’ sensitivity to tree width, with GPT-4o benefiting from wider search trees up to a point, while Claude-3.5-Sonnet’s performance degrades as tree width increases beyond 3.
